## Introduction

This assignment introduces **no new concepts**. Its goal is to consolidate everything from the previous assignments by building a small level with several AI agents that interact with each other and with the player.

Unlike the previous assignments, there are **no step-by-step instructions**. Each exercise states *what* the agent must do; you decide *how*, using the tools you already know. Hints point back to the assignment where the relevant concept was explained.

::: {.callout-note}
## Prerequisites
Assignments **01 (Basic Navigation)**, **02 (State Trees: Patrol and Chase)** and **03 (State Trees: AI Perception and EQS)**. Keep them open: you will need them.
:::

### What you can use

Everything below was covered before. If you feel you need something that is **not** in this table, stop and rethink the design: there is a solution that uses only these tools.

| Topic | Tools | Seen in |
|---|---|---|
| Navigation | Nav Mesh Bounds Volume, Nav Modifier Volume, Nav Area classes (incl. custom ones), Runtime Generation (*Dynamic*, *Dynamic Modifiers Only*) | 01 |
| Controllers | AIController vs. Character (brain vs. body), *On Possess* → *Start Logic* | 01, 02 |
| State Tree structure | Selection behaviors, enter conditions, transitions (*On Succeeded/Failed/Completed/Tick/Event*), Task Completion (*Any/All*) | 02 |
| State Tree data | Parameters, Context, Input/Output/Parameter categories, global tasks, bindings to AIController properties, property references (*Run Env Query → Result*) | 02, 03 |
| Custom nodes | `StateTreeTaskBlueprintBase`, `StateTreeConditionBlueprintBase` (with *Invert* via XOR) | 02 |
| Built-in tasks | *Move To*, *Delay*, *Debug Text*, *Run Env Query* | 02, 03 |
| Perception | AIPerception (Sight), *On Target Perception Updated / Forgotten*, *Break AIStimulus*, *Max Age*, *Get Currently Perceived Actors* | 03 |
| Events | Gameplay Tags, *Send State Tree Event* on the StateTreeAI component | 02 (Ex. 4), 03 |
| EQS | Pathing Grid generator, Trace and Distance tests, custom `EnvQueryContext_BlueprintBase`, run modes, EQS Testing Pawn | 03 |
| Debugging | Rewind Debugger, Gameplay Debugger (<span class="kbd">'</span>), *Debug Text*, *State Enabled*, Break On Enter/Exit | 02, 03 |

### The scenario

A small **warehouse** level. The player is a thief who must reach a few **loot** actors. The warehouse is protected by:

- a **Guard** that patrols hand-placed waypoints and chases the player;
- a **Lookout** that never fights, but raises the alarm and hides;
- (optional) a **Rat** that wanders around and runs from everyone.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Agents in the level and how they affect each other."
flowchart LR
    PLAYER(["Player<br/>(thief)"])
    GUARD["Guard<br/>waypoints · chase · search"]
    LOOK["Lookout<br/>watch · alarm · hide"]
    RAT["Rat (optional)<br/>wander · flee"]
    LOOK -- "sees player" --> PLAYER
    GUARD -- "sees / chases" --> PLAYER
    LOOK -. "alarm event<br/>(last known location)" .-> GUARD
    RAT -- "flees from" --> PLAYER
    RAT -- "flees from" --> GUARD
```

## Setup

1. Create a new **Third Person** (Blueprint) project named **`ST_Consolidation`**. Enable the **StateTree** and **Gameplay State Tree** plugins.
2. Build a simple warehouse in the default map: walls, a few rooms connected by doorways, crates (cubes) to hide behind, and at least one **sliding door** (a cube you can move at runtime).
3. Add a **Nav Mesh Bounds Volume** covering the whole level.
4. Create a folder `AI` with one sub-folder per agent: `AI/Guard`, `AI/Lookout`, `AI/Rat`, `AI/Shared`.
5. Put anything reused by more than one agent (tasks, conditions, EQS contexts, the waypoint actor) in `AI/Shared`.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Reuse first
Before writing a new task or condition, check whether one from Assignments 02 or 03 already does the job. `STT_FindRandomPosition`, `STC_InRange` and `EQS_FindHidingLocation` can all be copied into `AI/Shared` and reused, possibly with an extra parameter.
:::

## Part A — Navigation

### Exercise A1 — Terrain costs

Some floor areas are **oily**. Agents can walk on them, but prefer not to.

a. Create a custom Nav Area class `NavArea_Oil` with a **Default Cost** higher than 1, and place a few Nav Modifier Volumes using it.
b. Place an oily patch so that it is the **shortest** route between two rooms, with a longer clean route around it. Verify with <span class="kbd">P</span> and by watching an agent that it takes the clean route.
c. Find the cost value at which the agent switches from the oily route to the clean one. Write it down and explain why it is that value (path cost = sum of area costs, Assignment 01).

### Exercise A2 — The sliding door

a. The sliding door opens and closes every few seconds (a simple Timeline or *Set Actor Location* in the door's Blueprint is enough).
b. Attach a Nav Modifier component with **Null Area** to the door, so the closed door removes the nav mesh in the doorway.
c. Choose the cheapest **Runtime Generation** mode that still makes agents react to the door. Justify your choice in one sentence.

::: {.callout-note}
## Question A
Why is *Dynamic Modifiers Only* usually preferable to *Dynamic* in a shipped game? When would you still need *Dynamic*?
:::

## Part B — The Guard

Create `BP_Guard` (character), `AIC_Guard` (controller) and `ST_Guard` (State Tree). All decisions go in the **State Tree**; the controller only handles perception and forwards events.

### Exercise B1 — Waypoint patrol

a. Create a `BP_Waypoint` actor in `AI/Shared`. The guard has an **Instance Editable** array of waypoints, filled per instance in the level.
b. The guard walks the waypoints **in order**, waits 2 s at each one, and loops back to the first.
c. Add a tree parameter `bPingPong`. When `true`, the guard walks the list forwards and then backwards (1 → 2 → 3 → 2 → 1 …) instead of looping.
d. If a waypoint is unreachable (for example, behind the closed door), the guard skips it instead of getting stuck.

*Hints:* the current waypoint index must survive between states — think about where it can live (Assignment 03, *Outputs vs. parameters*). Use *Move To*'s failure to skip.

### Exercise B2 — Seeing the player

a. Give `AIC_Guard` an AIPerception component with Sight (Assignment 03 settings are a good start).
b. Use **events** (not *On Tick* polling) to switch between patrol and chase: `AI.Guard.PlayerSeen` / `AI.Guard.PlayerLost`.
c. While chasing, the guard **runs**; while patrolling, it **walks**; the speed changes **gradually** (Assignment 02, Exercise 2).
d. If there is no complete path to the player, the guard does **not** chase.

### Exercise B3 — Searching

When the guard loses sight of the player:

a. It moves to the player's **last known location** (*Stimulus Location*).
b. It then searches for **15 s**, visiting points around that location chosen by an **EQS** query (Pathing Grid around the last known location, not around the guard).
c. If it sees the player during the search, it chases again immediately.
d. When the search ends without finding the player, it returns to the **nearest** waypoint and resumes patrolling from there.

*Hints:* a parent state with a *Delay* of 15 s ends the search for all its children (Assignment 02, *Any active state can complete*). The query needs a context that returns a **location**, not an actor.

### Exercise B4 — Catch

When the guard reaches the player (distance < 150 uu):

a. Show `Caught!` above the guard for 2 s.
b. Teleport the player back to the **Player Start**.
c. The guard ignores the player for 5 s and then resumes patrolling.

## Part C — The Lookout

Create `BP_Lookout`, `AIC_Lookout` and `ST_Lookout`. The lookout stands on a fixed spot, turns slowly to watch the room, and never chases.

### Exercise C1 — Watch

a. The lookout alternates between **two or three look directions** (rotate in place, wait 3 s, rotate to the next one). Pick the order **at random** each time.
b. Its sight cone should be narrower but longer than the guard's.

### Exercise C2 — Raise the alarm

a. When the lookout sees the player, it shows `ALARM!` and sends an event to **every guard in the level** with the tag `AI.Guard.Alarm`.
b. The alarm must carry the **player's location**, and the guard must go straight to the **Search** behavior of Exercise B3 around that location, even if it never saw the player itself.
c. A guard that is **already chasing** ignores the alarm.

*Hints:* the guard's controller needs somewhere to store the received location before the event reaches its tree (Assignment 03, *Order matters*). Think about which State Tree states should have an *On Event* transition for the alarm, and which should not.

### Exercise C3 — Hide

After raising the alarm the lookout **hides** using an EQS query, like the Runner in Assignment 03, but with two changes:

a. The hiding spot must be at least **400 uu** from the player (filter, not score).
b. Prefer spots that are **close to a guard** (score). Write a context that returns all guards' locations or the nearest guard.
c. When the player has been out of sight for 10 s, the lookout walks back to its watch spot and resumes watching.

*Hint:* the 10 s can come from *Max Age* and *On Target Perception Forgotten*.

## Part D — The Rat (optional)

Create `BP_Rat` (a scaled-down character is fine) and `ST_Rat`.

a. The rat wanders to random points, **avoiding oily areas** even more than the other agents do (think about where in Assignment 01 per-agent area costs were mentioned).
b. It perceives **both the player and the guards**, and flees from whichever it sees, using an EQS query that scores points far from **all** perceived threats.
c. Use **utility-based selection** to choose between *Wander*, *Flee* and *Rest* (rest becomes more attractive the longer the rat has been running).

## Part E — Debugging challenge

Your colleague built the State Tree below for a guard. Each line describes a symptom they observed. For each one, **find the cause** and **describe the fix** (no need to implement it). All causes are things that were discussed in Assignments 02 and 03.

```
Root  (Try Select Children In Order)   Global task: STT_CheckLOS
├── Chase   Enter: STT_FindTarget.Target is valid
│   Tasks: STT_FindTarget, Move To (Target)
├── Patrol  (Try Select Children In Order)
│   ├── MoveToWaypoint   Tasks: STT_NextWaypoint, Move To
│   └── Wait             Task: Delay 2 s
└── Idle    Task: Delay 5 s
```

| # | Symptom |
|---|---|
| 1 | The guard **never** enters *Chase*, even when the player stands right in front of it. |
| 2 | Every few seconds the whole tree **stops**; the guard freezes until the level is restarted. |
| 3 | The guard walks to the first waypoint, waits, and then goes to the **same** waypoint again forever. |
| 4 | `STT_NextWaypoint` doesn't show its `Waypoints` variable in the State Tree editor. |
| 5 | The controller sends `AI.Guard.PlayerSeen`, the Rewind Debugger shows the event arriving, but no transition fires. |
| 6 | After moving *MoveToWaypoint* above *Wait*, the guard sometimes interrupts its wait and walks off early. *(Hint: look at what the tasks on Patrol would do.)* |

## Part F — Questions

Answer briefly (a few sentences each) in your report.

1. In Exercise B2 you used events instead of *On Tick* transitions. Give one situation in this level where **polling** would have been the simpler choice.
2. Which data in your solution lives in **tree parameters**, which in **task outputs**, and which in the **AI Controller**? Justify one choice of each.
3. Where did you put the guard's speed logic (task in a state, global task, Character Blueprint)? What are the trade-offs?
4. Your Search state (Exercise B3) and the Lookout's Hide state both use EQS. Compare the two queries: generator, contexts, tests and run mode.
5. If you had to add a second guard type that does everything the guard does but never searches, how would you avoid duplicating `ST_Guard`?

## Deliverables

- The Unreal project (without `Intermediate`, `Saved`, `DerivedDataCache` and `Binaries` folders).
- A short video (≤ 3 min) showing each exercise working, with the Gameplay Debugger or *Debug Text* making the active states visible.
- A short report (PDF or Markdown) with:
  - a diagram of each State Tree (states, enter conditions, transitions);
  - the answers to **Question A**, **Part E** and **Part F**.
